Consult Summary:
- Telehealth consult for acute-onset shortness of breath in a 4-weeks postpartum patient after cesarean section.
- Clinician expressed concern for venous thromboembolism (possible pulmonary embolism). Patient advised to attend hospital urgently; elected to self-present.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute shortness of breath: Began ~1 hour prior to call while at rest (watching TV); new symptom. Associated symptoms: palpitations (“heart really going”), nonproductive cough (started yesterday), chest soreness with deep inspiration. No chest pain at rest reported.
- Postpartum risk factor: Cesarean section 4 weeks ago; incision site tender.
- Family history: Mother had leg clots.
- Examination (telehealth): Patient counted 30 beats during clinician-timed interval (duration not specified); clinician assessed heart rate as “slightly fast.”
- Clinical impression: Concern for venous thromboembolism (possible PE). Advised urgent hospital assessment.
- Differential discussed: Clots in legs or lungs (DVT/PE).

Issue 2:
- Post-cesarean recovery: 4 weeks postpartum, tender C-section scar. Used codeine for postoperative pain regularly but not taken for ~1 week. No other postoperative medications reported.

Issue 3:
- Acute cough: Onset yesterday; dry (no sputum). No fever or other infectious symptoms documented.

Medications:
- Codeine (dose/route/frequency not documented); previously taken regularly post-op; not taken for ~1 week. Advised not to take currently.

Allergies:
- Ibuprofen (reaction not recalled; details not documented).

Past Medical History:
- Cesarean section 4 weeks ago.
- No other medical problems reported.

Social History:
- Lives with newborn; currently at home alone with baby. Partner at work.
- Tobacco/alcohol/substance use not documented.

Preventative History:
- Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- Telehealth only.
- Heart rate: Patient counted 30 beats during clinician-timed interval (timing not specified); clinician described as “slightly fast.”
- No other vitals or physical findings documented.

Plan:
- Immediate hospital evaluation to rule out venous thromboembolism (possible PE/DVT). Patient to self-transport promptly and bring baby essentials.
- Avoid codeine for now.
- Hospital to provide further diagnostics and treatment as indicated (e.g., therapy to reduce clot if confirmed).

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Full vitals, detailed ROS (fever, leg pain/swelling, hemoptysis), obstetric/postpartum complications review, complete medication list and reconciliation, details of ibuprofen allergy reaction, smoking/alcohol history, follow-up plan post-hospital visit.
- Internal conflicts: Date of birth reported as April 20, 1980 by patient; clinician later stated 1983 (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor pauses/ellipses but no significant audio issues noted.
